user.title: Location
user.description: Which location should warnings be watched for?

menu_options.home: Use my Home Assistant home location

zone.title: Zone
zone.description: Warnings are shown for every area the zone's circle touches, up to a radius of 50 km. Moving or resizing the zone updates this location. A large radius, or one near the coast, also reaches coastal waters, so marine wind and surf warnings can apply.

error.no_area: The Bureau of Meteorology has no warning areas at this location. Check that it is in Australia.
error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the Bureau of Meteorology. Try again later.
error.zone_not_found: That zone no longer exists. Pick another one.

abort.no_area: The Bureau of Meteorology has no warning areas at your home location. Enter a location in Australia instead.
abort.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to the Bureau of Meteorology. Try again later.

refresh_failing.title: Cannot reach the Bureau of Meteorology
refresh_failing.description:
BoM Warnings could not fetch warnings from the Bureau of Meteorology for the last 3 refreshes, so its entities are unavailable and no warnings will be reported until this clears.

This usually means Home Assistant cannot reach the Bureau's FTP server (ftp.bom.gov.au, port 21), or the server is down.

To fix it:
1. Check that Home Assistant has internet access.
2. Check that your firewall, router or DNS filter allows outgoing FTP to ftp.bom.gov.au on port 21.
3. Check whether the Bureau's website is reporting an outage.
4. Nothing more is needed once it is fixed: the integration retries every 10 minutes and this issue clears by itself when a refresh succeeds.

If it persists, download the diagnostics from the BoM Warnings integration page and include them in a bug report.

no_area.title: No warning area for {title}
no_area.description: After the Bureau of Meteorology updated its area boundaries, {title} is no longer inside any warning area, so its saved areas are being kept. Remove this location and add it again with coordinates inside Australia.

zone_removed.title: Zone for {title} was deleted
zone_removed.description:
The zone {zone} that {title} follows no longer exists, so {title} is staying on the warning areas it last had and will not follow any further changes.

To fix it, either:
- Create a zone with the same name again in Settings > Areas, labels & zones > Zones. This location picks it up and this notice clears by itself.
- Remove this location and add it again, choosing another zone.

radius_clamped.title: Zone radius for {title} is too large
radius_clamped.description:
The zone behind {title} has a radius of {radius} km. BoM Warnings only looks {max} km around the centre, because a larger circle would list warnings for most of a state. Warnings beyond {max} km are not shown.

To clear this notice, reduce the zone's radius to {max} km or less in Settings > Areas, labels & zones > Zones.

init.title: Warnings I care about

data_description.hide_final_cancelled: Hide a warning once it has ended or been cancelled. This is about a warning's phase, not its type.
data_description.warning_types: Tick the types that matter here. Severe weather also covers Coastal Hazard Warnings, so it suits a dashboard better than an automation. Marine wind means coastal and local waters, not wind at your house, and Hazardous surf is for the coast the location reaches; both need a zone whose circle reaches the sea. Other warnings covers any type without its own entry, such as tsunami, and any type BoM adds later.

init.description: Choose the warning types that matter for this location. A type that is on counts everywhere (the warning sensor, the count, the most severe warning and the events) and has its own sensor. A type that is off is ignored everywhere and its sensor is removed. Marine wind and Hazardous surf only apply when the location reaches the sea, so use a zone with a large enough radius.
